blocks.md: The Earth has three main layers. The thin outer **crust** is solid rock. Below it is the **mantle**, very hot and partly molten. At the centre is the **core**, made mostly of iron and nickel. The crust is broken into large pieces called **plates** that move very slowly. Where plates meet, collide or separate, we find most **volcanoes**, **earthquakes** and **fold mountains**.

blocks.caption: A volcano in cross-section
blocks.alt: A cone-shaped volcano with a crater, a vent leading down to a magma chamber.

blocks.title: Volcano
blocks.md: A **volcano** is an opening in the crust through which **magma** (called **lava** when it reaches the surface), gas and ash escape. Magma rises from the **magma chamber** through the **vent** and leaves by the **crater**. Layers of lava and ash build up a **cone**. A volcano can be **active**, **dormant** (asleep) or **extinct** (dead).

blocks.title: Earthquake
blocks.md: An **earthquake** is a shaking of the ground caused by sudden movement of rocks along cracks called faults. The point underground where it starts is the **focus**; the point on the surface above it is the **epicentre**. A **seismograph** records the waves. Effects: collapsed buildings, landslides, fires and, at sea, huge waves called **tsunamis**.

**Cameroon.** Mount Cameroon, in the South-West, is an active volcano that has erupted several times in modern times. It belongs to the **Cameroon Volcanic Line**, a chain that includes Mount Manengouba, the Bamboutos and Mount Oku. In 1986 a huge release of carbon dioxide gas from the crater **Lake Nyos** killed many people, a reminder that volcanic regions bring hazards as well as fertile soils and beautiful scenery.

blocks.title: Be careful
blocks.md:
- Magma is underground; lava is magma on the surface.
- The focus is under the ground; the epicentre is on the surface.
- A volcano that is quiet is not always extinct: dormant volcanoes can erupt again.

blocks.title: Example 1: focus and epicentre
blocks.statement: An earthquake starts 10 km below the surface. What is the point on the surface directly above called?
steps: The origin underground is the focus.
The place directly above it on the surface is where shaking is strongest.

blocks.title: Example 2: advantages and risks
blocks.statement: Give one benefit and one risk of living near a volcano.
steps: Volcanic rock weathers into fertile soil.
An eruption can send lava, ash and gas over farms and homes.
So the benefit is fertile soil and the risk is eruption.
